Now I can see the pattern. At line 311, for DataArrays: `attrs = merge_attrs([x.attrs for x in objs], ...)`. The `objs` list is built from `_all_of_type(args, DataArray)` — only actual DataArray objects have `.attrs`, so scalars are excluded from `objs`. 

Similarly at line 764 for Variables: `[obj.attrs for obj in objs]` where `objs = _all_of_type(args, Variable)`.

So when `x` is a scalar (like `1`), it's not a DataArray/Variable, so `objs` only contains the non-scalar arguments. The `attrs` list passed to the `keep_attrs` callable will have fewer entries than the 3 arguments to `where`, and `attrs[1]` can be out of range.

The fix correctly handles this by returning an empty dict `{}` when there aren't enough entries in the attrs list — which is the right behavior since a scalar has no attributes to preserve.

The fix is a one-line change in `xarray/core/computation.py:1832`: the `keep_attrs` lambda now checks `len(attrs) > 1` before accessing `attrs[1]`, falling back to an empty dict `{}` when scalars cause the attrs list to be shorter than expected.
